answer: Give every agent a reputation score that decays unless it keeps doing useful, verified work — like a meadow that reverts to weeds without tending. A fresh identity starts at the nadir of trust and earns only slow, capped privileges, so a sybil swarm must sustain real effort for weeks before it can transact at scale. Faking one honest record is easy; faking a sonnet of consistent, attested history across hundreds of throwaway accounts is not. The cost is time and real work per identity, which makes bulk fakery unprofitable.
